hero.heading: SaaS development from the first paying workflow.
hero.subtitle: Accounts, permissions, billing, and the screens that deliver the product. Built so the second customer is not a special case.

overview: A SaaS build is the product loop: sign up, do the valuable thing, pay, and come back. I build that loop before the surrounding dashboards.
problem: Early SaaS products collect screens. Billing is a mock, permissions are an if-statement, and the first real customer forces a rewrite.
solution: I start with tenancy, auth, and the core workflow. Stripe billing is real. The admin view is only what you need to support customers.

faqs.question: Do you build the whole company, or the product?
faqs.answer: The product. Marketing sites can be part of the same codebase when you want them, but the priority is the thing customers log into.

faqs.question: Which database do you use?
faqs.answer: PostgreSQL is the default. If you already run something else, I will use it when it fits.
